title: Home broadband serviceability and experiment request
not_questions: The address lookup remains in the existing ordering platform and Akamai serves our public pages.
We will not license Real-Time CDP for the broadband pilot.
Use orderable addresses as the denominator throughout the response.
never_in_text: Home broadband serviceability and experiment request

questions.text: Describe how AEM Sites would present an ambiguous apartment match without promising that a service visit can be booked.
Explain which AEM Sites content Akamai may cache when neighboring addresses have different broadband availability.
Provide an AEM Sites publishing workflow for a neighborhood build delay, including the evidence an editor needs before restoring an installation date.
Show how AEM Sites would preserve a customer's selected language when a serviceability check sends them back to the address form.
Describe an Adobe Target experiment comparing two installation appointment messages for eligible fiber addresses only.
Define an Adobe Target holdout for households already participating in our technician callback trial and show how staff can verify the exclusion.
Explain how our analyst would monitor an Adobe Target experiment if an outage temporarily prevents customers in one neighborhood from ordering.
Set out the Adobe Target stopping rule and the records required before we apply the winning appointment message to newly connected streets.
Name the delivery manager and the on-call lead your firm can supply during the first weekend of the pilot.
Describe one comparable telecom engagement and give a contact who can confirm your responsibility for the address eligibility work.
Provide your rate for a deferred neighborhood release and state how much notice avoids a cancellation charge.
List the subcontractors that would access customer addresses and identify the contract owner accountable for each one.
